name: LLM Privacy Challenge
description: The NeurIPS 2024 LLM Privacy Challenge addresses privacy risks in Large Language Models (LLMs) by focusing on identifying vulnerabilities (Red Team) and developing protective measures (Blue Team). Participants work with synthetic datasets to explore privacy-preserving techniques.

cr:input.name: Synthetic Private Data
cr:input.description: Synthetic datasets designed to mimic real-world private information, such as replacing private data in public datasets (e.g., Enron emails) with random strings while maintaining realistic formats. These datasets are large, diverse, and ethically generated.
cr:input.contentUrl: [FILL IN THE BLANK: dataset download URL]

cr:output.name: predictions
cr:output.description: The expected output includes attack results (e.g., extracted sensitive information) for Red Team and defense results (e.g., sanitized outputs or privacy-preserving measures) for Blue Team.

field.name: attack_accuracy
field.description: The success rate of identifying and extracting sensitive information from LLMs. Example: 0.85 for 85% accuracy.

field.name: efficiency
field.description: Resource efficiency of the method, such as the number of tokens or queries used for Red Team or computational overhead for Blue Team. Example: 0.75 for 75% efficiency.

field.name: model_effectiveness
field.description: The general performance of the LLM after applying defensive methods (Blue Team only). Example: 0.92 for 92% effectiveness.

cr:evaluation.notes: Red Team submissions are ranked higher for higher attack accuracy and efficiency. Blue Team submissions are ranked higher for lower attack accuracy, higher efficiency, and better model effectiveness.
